Do you think a million-dollar term life insurance policy sounds like too much insurance?

As a Certified Financial Planner, I see underinsured people every day.

A million-dollar term life insurance policy might actually be the minimum coverage needed for the typical middle-class household, but it’s affordable.

That might sound like an exaggeration, but if you crunch the numbers – just as we’ll be doing a little bit – you’ll realize that a million-dollar policy might be just what you need.

The good news is term life insurance isn’t nearly as costly as most people think.

What makes term life insurance even better is that larger policies cost less on a per thousand basis than smaller policies do. You may find the premium on a $1 million policy is only a little bit higher than it is for $500,000.

It has been revealed that probably, but let’s find out. A general rule of thumb is that you should get 10x your income as baseline coverage for life insurance.

If you’re young, that may be low because you may want to provide your family with enough to replace your income for 15 years or more.

It has been revealed that today, $1 million has become the latest baseline for life insurance by a primary breadwinner. Anything less could leave your family financially impaired.

Here’s a list of all the different obligations you may want to have life insurance cover in the unfortunate event you pass away early.

Now that you have an idea of these obligations, let’s punch them into this life insurance calculator to find out if you need a million-dollar policy.

Sources indicate that according to Policy Genius, the average cost for a 20-year $1 million term life insurance policy for a 35-year-old male is $53 per month. However, your rate will vary according to the following factors.

The best, and easiest place to start is online. I recommend having two or three insurers compete for your business to make sure you get the best rate and coverage. To see how cheap term life can be, choose your state from the map above to be matched with top life insurance providers instantly.

Let’s look at the individual components that can quickly add up to over a million-dollar policy.

It has been revealed that this is where things can get a bit intimidating. Even if you earn a modest income, you may need close to $1 million to replace that income after your death in order to provide for your family’s basic living expenses.

The conventional wisdom in the insurance industry is that you should maintain a life insurance policy equal to between 10 times and 20 times your annual income. So if you earn around $50K per year, that would mean policy coverage between $500K and $1 million.

The complication today is that with interest rates being as low as they are that might not be enough either.

For example, if you have a $1 million policy that could be invested at 5% per year, your family could live on the interest earned – which conveniently comes to $50,000 per year – for the next 20 years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some substantial companies pay every dollar of tuition at their partner schools, even for part-time workers starting on day one, and others pay up to a set amount each year. Before you take a job for the benefit, check which schools and degrees it covers and whether you’d owe the money back if you leave.

Chosen for that benefit, an hourly job can be a debt-free route to a degree.

The benefits come in two kinds. The most generous pay all of the tuition, though only at partner schools and usually only for programs in the tech giant’s catalog, and a few start the day you’re hired. The rest pay up to a set amount, often $5,250 a year, and you cover anything above it. At many of these employers, part-time workers qualify too.

Start with the catalog. A full-tuition benefit pays only at its partner schools and for the programs on its list, so find the degree you want there, and note how long you’d work before you can enroll.

Then ask whether you’d owe any of the money back if you left. Walmart and Starbucks don’t require you to stay after you finish, while McDonald’s makes managers who miss its transcript deadlines repay the money.

It has been revealed that last, make sure the degree pays. The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Occupational Outlook Handbook lists each job’s median pay and the education it usually takes, so look up the job you want before you pick a program. If you already owe student loans, also ask whether the employer pays toward them, a separate benefit some companies offer.

It has been revealed that take a part-time Walmart cashier with no college credits who earns an online bachelor’s degree from Southern Newly introduced Hampshire University, a Live Better U partner. Walmart’s benefit leaves her little or nothing to pay for tuition and required books. Paying her own way, she’d owe SNHU’s online rate of $354 a credit for 120 credits, or $42,480. Say she borrowed it at 6.52%, the rate Federal Student Aid set for new undergraduate loans for 2026-27, with no interest added while she’s in school. Repaid over 10 years, that’s about $483 a month, or about $15,450 in interest.

Before you accept an offer, ask the recruiter for the benefit’s written terms and its list of partner schools, then enroll in a covered program as soon as you’re eligible.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that keeping most of your savings in a few stocks makes sense for firm founders and full-time investors. For everyone else, one company’s collapse can erase years of saving. Diversify by owning thousands of stocks of every size and sector through one low-cost total-market or total-world index fund, and skip extra funds that hold the same companies.

According to recent reports, enron, Lehman Brothers, and General Electric were household names, and each company’s stock fell 90% or more from its high. Anyone holding little besides one of them had lost most of their savings at the low, and Enron and Lehman went bankrupt.

It has been revealed that A founder can keep a fortune in one stock because they run the company. Warren Buffett’s case against diversifying is for experts. In a 1993 shareholder letter, he wrote that owning many stocks makes no sense for investors who understand businesses well enough to find five to 10 fairly priced companies with lasting advantages. Everyone else, he wrote, should own many stocks, such as through an index fund.

Finance professor Hendrik Bessembinder found that four of every seven U.S. stocks since 1926 earned less over their lifetimes than one-month Treasury bills, short-term loans to the government. The best-performing 4% of companies produced all of the market’s gain over those bills, since the rest together only matched them. A handful of stocks will probably miss that 4%, and a fund that owns the whole market holds all of it.

Diversifying protects you from one company, industry, or country going bad, not from a falling market. The S&P 500, an index of 500 large U.S. companies, lost about 37% in 2008 including dividends.

Diversifying costs almost nothing. One fund, Vanguard Total World Stock ETF, holds more than 10,000 stocks in the U.S. and abroad for 0.06% a year, or $6 on every $10,000. A total-market fund covers thousands of U.S. stocks.

Industry observers note that choose an index fund, not an actively managed fund whose manager picks the stocks, and keep any stocks you buy on your own to a small slice of your portfolio. If your job gives you company shares, cap your employer’s stock too.

The opposite mistake is owning several funds that hold the same companies. FINRA, the brokerage industry’s regulator, suggests checking whether your funds hold similar companies. Look up each fund’s 10 largest holdings on its own page, and when the same names top two lists, one total-market fund can replace both.

Buy that fund through one of the best online brokers.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

It has been revealed that one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

Meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that shows you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

According to recent reports, plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

In a recent development, if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

Recent findings suggest that most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal plans start at $3 per month, while a family proposal costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

The best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

In a recent development, earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

In a recent development, where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

Recent findings suggest that if you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Industry observers note that starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

That mentioned, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

It has been revealed that how much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

Recent findings suggest that donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

Industry observers note that that said, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

Recent findings suggest that if you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, upgrade a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

If you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

It has been revealed that another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

In a recent development, unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

Industry observers note that finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

You won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, online stores reprice items as demand, stock, and rivals’ prices change, and some also use your location or browsing history to set the price you see. Before you buy, check the item at another store and in a logged-out private window, then set a price alert instead of guessing when the price will drop.

In a recent development, from one screen, you can’t tell whether a price jumped for every shopper or just for you. Both happen, and the second has been documented for over a decade.

In 2012, The Wall Street Journal found Staples’ website showing one shopper a stapler for $15.79 and another, a few miles away, the same stapler for $14.29. The lower price usually went to shoppers the site judged to be within about 20 miles of an OfficeMax or Office Depot store. In January 2025, the Federal Trade Commission published first findings from its study of the firms retailers hire to set prices. Details like your precise location or browsing history can often be used to give you a different price than other shoppers get for the same goods, the agency found.

Industry observers note that in Upcoming York, the Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act requires a store that sets a price from your personal data to say so with the notice “This price was set by an algorithm using your personal data.” Since Oct. 1, 2026, a Maryland law has barred large grocers and grocery delivery services from using personal data to charge shoppers more for groceries.

Before you pay, run three checks:.

A price alert beats refreshing the page, since you can’t predict when software working from data you never see will cut the price. Google Shopping’s price tracking emails you when the price drops below a target you choose, so base that target on the item’s price history.

Set up your first price alert on Google Shopping.

Pet Food Cost per Day – The Pricier Bag Can Be Cheaper to Feed

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the cheaper bag of pet food isn’t always the cheaper one to feed.
  • The price per pound on a shelf tag misses how long each pound lasts.
  • Industry observers note that take two 30-pound bags for a 50-pound dog, at illustrative prices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the cheaper bag of pet food isn’t always the cheaper one to feed. A denser food holds more calories in each cup, so your pet eats less of it and the bag lasts longer. Before you buy or switch, divide each bag’s price by the days it lasts at your pet’s feeding amount.

The price per pound on a shelf tag misses how long each pound lasts. A pound of a calorie-dense food feeds your pet for more days than a pound of a less dense one.

Industry observers note that take two 30-pound bags for a 50-pound dog, at illustrative prices. One costs $45 and lasts the dog 40 days. The other, a denser food, costs $52 and lasts 47 days. Per pound, the denser food costs $1.73 and the other $1.50. Per day, the denser food costs about $1.11 and the other about $1.13, so the $52 bag costs less to feed than the $45 bag.

Gaps like that grow with how much your pet eats, so they matter most for substantial dogs. A gap of 10 cents a day comes to $36.50 a year.

To compare two dry foods this way:.

Newer labels list a cup’s weight in grams instead of kcal/kg. To get kcal/kg from those, multiply the calories per cup by 1,000 and divide by that weight. For canned food, divide your pet’s daily calories by the calories per can, then multiply by the price per can.

Sources indicate that between two sizes of the same food, every pound holds the same calories, so the lower price per pound settles it. The bigger bag’s saving depends on the food staying fresh. A veterinary nutritionist at Tufts University recommends finishing an opened bag within two to three months, so buy the size your pet empties in that time.

In a recent development, switch to a latest food slowly. Mix a little more of it into the old food each day for at least a week.

In a recent development, having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

In a recent development, if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That mentioned, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

In a recent development, you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

No matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data shows the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

To save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

The next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment intends.

If you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment plans and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

In a recent development, then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

According to recent reports, it’s crucial to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as quickly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

In a recent development, finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

Recent findings suggest that how much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

It has been revealed that having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete plan that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

Recent findings suggest that in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun new way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which remarked something like,.

According to recent reports, “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

Recent findings suggest that okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

So I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

One of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

Sources indicate that but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

It has been revealed that I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

Then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

But eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

Admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

Then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

It has been revealed that it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

Sources indicate that experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning upcoming things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

One interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

Thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

According to recent reports, so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

And of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

As with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

We will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

*(Vine Gold is not all that useful as it turns out as 99.9% of the available items seem to be the same trinkets you see in the Silver tier).

** What about the Heated Vest that started it all? Well, I still love that thing and now that fall is coming back it is already helping me be warmer in a cooler house. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Walmart clearance sticker keeps the price it was printed with, and the store may have marked the item down again since.
  • Walmart claims each store’s manager can cut prices to clear out extra stock, and that changing prices on paper tags by hand could take hours or even days.
  • Walmart is replacing its paper shelf tags with digital labels that show the same price the register charges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Walmart clearance sticker keeps the price it was printed with, and the store may have marked the item down again since. Scan the item with the free Walmart app while you’re in the store. The app shows that store’s current price, and that’s what you’ll pay at the register.

Walmart claims each store’s manager can cut prices to clear out extra stock, and that changing prices on paper tags by hand could take hours or even days. The register charges the new price in the meantime.

Walmart is replacing its paper shelf tags with digital labels that show the same price the register charges. It remarked in March 2026 that it expects every U.S. store to have them within a year. A clearance sticker on the item itself is still paper, though, so it’s the likeliest place to find an old price, along with the shelf tags in any store that hasn’t switched yet.

Say a pair of kids’ sneakers carries a $14.97 clearance sticker, and the store has since cut the price to $5. The sticker still notes $14.97, but the app shows $5, and $5 is what you’ll pay.

Recent findings suggest that look for clearance stickers on the displays at the ends of aisles, along the back wall of each department, and in the seasonal aisle the week after a holiday. Open the app inside the store with location sharing on, since it demonstrates in-store prices only once it knows you’re there. Then tap the scanner icon in the search bar and scan the product’s own barcode, not one printed for shipping or storage.

The price you see applies only at that store. Walmart says prices can vary from store to store and that it doesn’t price match its own stores, so the store won’t match a lower price you found at another Walmart. Clearance is also whatever the store has left, so an item you pass up today may be gone the next time you come in.

For a substantial purchase you can time, like a TV or a mattress, skip the clearance hunt and wait for its category’s yearly sale season.

Scan every clearance sticker before the item goes in your cart, and buy what scans at a price you’d pay.

Download the free Walmart app and sign in before your next trip.

Used Books for a Few Dollars – Compare Prices With Shipping, Then Check Library Sales

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Before you buy a print book newly introduced, look for a used copy, which often costs a few dollars.
  • Recent findings suggest that A hardcover that costs $30 newly introduced can cost $2 at a library sale or $6 with shipping from an online used-book seller.
  • On a marketplace like AbeBooks, each seller sets its own shipping charge, so a $1 copy with $4 shipping costs more than a $4 copy that ships free.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before you buy a print book newly introduced, look for a used copy, which often costs a few dollars. Online, compare sellers by what you’d pay with shipping, not the listed price. Then check library book sales near you, where many books cost even less.

Recent findings suggest that A hardcover that costs $30 newly introduced can cost $2 at a library sale or $6 with shipping from an online used-book seller. Books hold up well, so a used copy in good condition reads just like a new one.

Online, the catch is shipping. On a marketplace like AbeBooks, each seller sets its own shipping charge, so a $1 copy with $4 shipping costs more than a $4 copy that ships free. BookFinder.com compares offers from more than 100,000 booksellers, and its searches take shipping into account. Search the title there before you buy anywhere.

ThriftBooks, which sells millions of used books, charges nothing for standard shipping on a US order over $15, so buying several books at once can cost less than ordering them one at a time.

Industry observers note that locally, browse used bookstores and thrift stores, and watch for library book sales. The library’s Friends group, which raises money for the library, often runs the sale, and hardcovers commonly cost $1 to $3. Many end with a bag sale, when a full bag often costs $5 or $10. Find one on your library’s website or on Book Sale Finder, which lists library and other nonprofit book sales by state. Some libraries also keep a sale shelf or a Friends bookstore open between sales.

Sources indicate that before you pay, check the condition grade. ThriftBooks’ grades run from Like Newly introduced down to Acceptable, and AbeBooks’ guide describes a Good copy as one with average wear and every text page intact. That’s usually good enough for a book you’ll read rather than display. Ex-library copies, former library books that often carry stamps and stickers, usually cost less. To get a particular edition, search by its ISBN, the number assigned to each edition and format of a book. A hardcover and a paperback of the same title each have their own.

Trade in the books you won’t reread at a used bookstore that buys them, and ask for store credit, which is often worth at least 20% more than the cash offer.

Sources indicate that certificates of Deposit (CDs) work similarly to online savings accounts or money market accounts in terms of offering great returns with zero risk. The difference is, CDs “lock your money up” for a specified period of time. To access your funds before the term ends, you’ll have to pay a penalty.

Although CDs offer less liquidity than a regular checking account or savings account, you might get a higher rate of return with this financial product. This is especially true if you open a CD account with a longer timeline; for example, a 60-month CD instead of a 12-month CD.

According to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), national average CD rates range from 0.23% to 1.81% depending on the CD term, as of writing.

  • In a recent development, in each food’s biggest bag at Walmart, the store’s own Pure Balance Chicken & Brown Rice Recipe costs $1.17 a pound, less than half the $2.67 a pound for Blue Buffalo’s Wilderness Grain-Free Chicken Recipe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, before paying extra for premium dog or cat food, find the small-print line on the package that names your pet’s life stage and AAFCO, the group that sets pet food nutrient standards. Any food with that line meets the same standards as pricier brands, so buy the cheapest one your pet does well on.

In a recent development, in each food’s biggest bag at Walmart, the store’s own Pure Balance Chicken & Brown Rice Recipe costs $1.17 a pound, less than half the $2.67 a pound for Blue Buffalo’s Wilderness Grain-Free Chicken Recipe. Both dry dog foods carry that line and have nearly the same calories per pound.

Industry observers note that that line is the nutritional adequacy statement, and newer labels add a short version on the front, such as Complete Food for Adult Dogs. The statement says the food was formulated to meet the nutrient standards of the Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO) or passed AAFCO feeding trials. It also names a life stage, such as growth for puppies and kittens, adult maintenance, or all life stages. The FDA says a food has to pass one of those tests to be called complete and balanced, which means it’s meant to be your pet’s only food. One labeled for intermittent or supplemental feeding only isn’t a complete diet.

Recent findings suggest that premium claims don’t make a food more complete. Natural describes how ingredients are sourced and processed, organic how they’re grown, and human-grade how the food and its ingredients are handled. Grain-free isn’t healthier for most pets either. Veterinary nutritionists at Tufts University call it a marketing concept and say grain allergies are rare.

The FDA has also investigated reports of a heart disease called dilated cardiomyopathy in dogs eating certain foods, many of them grain-free. It hasn’t established that the foods cause the disease, but ask your vet before switching your dog to grain-free.

According to recent reports, so compare prices only among foods whose statement names your pet’s life stage, and look at dry food first. In a Tufts price check of cat foods, even the most expensive dry food cost less per day than the cheapest canned one, for the same calories.

If you’d rather cook, have a veterinary nutritionist write the recipe for any homemade dog food or cat food you’d serve daily.

For a grown dog or cat, a store brand whose statement covers adult maintenance or all life stages is a complete diet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before you buy a bigger item upcoming on Amazon, check Amazon Resale, formerly Amazon Warehouse. Amazon sells inspected returns and open-box goods there below the new price, with its usual return policy. Read the condition grade first, since a lower grade can mean missing accessories or parts, and buy only when the discount covers their cost.

One product can be listed on Resale in several grades at once, each at its own price.

Sources indicate that amazon inspects each item before giving it one of four grades, and it tests electronics and resets them to factory settings. A Like New item works perfectly and has every essential accessory, though its packaging may be damaged. A Very Good one may show light use and minor cosmetic flaws, and it can lack non-essential accessories.

In a recent development, A Good item can show wear from moderate use, and an Acceptable one can show clear signs of use, such as scratches and dents. Either may be missing accessories or parts you’d have to buy before you can use it, and the listing’s description names anything missing.

To find offers, browse Amazon Resale by category, or look on a regular product page for the Save with Used or Buy Used section and open See details to compare grades. Resale purchases fall under Amazon’s return policy, which gives most items 30 days. Each item is one of a kind, though, so Amazon can’t swap a disappointing one for another in exactly the same condition. Test your item the day it arrives.

According to recent reports, check the maker’s warranty too. Under FTC rules, a written warranty on a product over $15 must say so if it covers only the original buyer, which may not be you. For a laptop or phone you’d want covered by a warranty, look at refurbished electronics sold with one instead.

Say a stand mixer is listed as Like Latest at 20% below the new price because a buyer opened the box and sent it back. Every essential accessory is included, so you get a fully working mixer for 20% less, in an opened box. At a lower grade with the bowl missing, the discount has to cover a new bowl before it saves you anything.

Like Newly introduced and Very Good are the grades to start with, since neither can be missing anything the item needs to work.

Search Amazon Resale for the next bigger item on your shopping list.

  • Lenders read that report before they approve you or set your rate, and landlords, insurers, and phone companies can check it too.
  • Paying with a debit card isn’t borrowing, so that spending normally doesn’t show up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your credit report lists your loans and cards with their balances, limits, and payment history, plus any collections, any bankruptcy, and the companies that have checked it. Your income, savings, and credit score aren’t on it. Pull your free reports and read each section for accounts you didn’t open, wrong balances, and on-time payments marked late.

Lenders read that report before they approve you or set your rate, and landlords, insurers, and phone companies can check it too. Seeing it first lets you catch a mistake before it costs you.

The report covers credit only. Paying with a debit card isn’t borrowing, so that spending normally doesn’t show up. Your score is calculated from the report but isn’t part of it. Since April 2023, the three credit bureaus have also stopped listing any medical bill sent to collectors that’s been paid off, was under $500 when first reported, or is less than a year past due.

In a recent development, negative items don’t stay for good. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau states most, like late payments, can be reported for up to seven years, and a bankruptcy for up to 10.

Read each of your free reports one section at a time:.

Recent findings suggest that not every surprise is a problem. A first-time reader might find a store card she forgot, still open at a $0 balance. That card has been helping her, since an open account with no missed payments keeps adding to the length of her credit history.

Dispute any entry that’s wrong, not just forgotten.

Checking your own reports never lowers your score, so read them now, well before a lender does.

Join Target Circle free, then enter your phone number or scan the Target app’s Wallet barcode at every checkout, since its deals come off automatically only for members who identify themselves. Before each trip, open the app to activate your bonuses and add manufacturer coupons, which never apply on their own.

In a recent development, those steps matter more since April 2024, when Target relaunched Target Circle and dropped its 1% back on purchases. Now a member who doesn’t identify at checkout gets nothing from the program.

The relaunch also ended the old routine of tapping to save each offer, though bonuses and the manufacturer coupons in the app still need that tap. Bonuses are personalized offers that vary from member to member. Some take money off. Others pay Target Circle Rewards, credit you can spend on a later trip, once you reach a spending total or use a service like Order Pickup. Rewards expire if you go a year without earning or redeeming any.

Industry observers note that the coupons are worth adding because they come off on top of the automatic deals. Target’s coupon policy allows one manufacturer coupon per item alongside its own offers, so a bottle of detergent with a 20%-off Circle deal and a $1 manufacturer coupon you added gets both discounts at checkout.

Make sure your Target account has two details:.

Two other products carry the Circle name. The Target Circle Credit Card takes another 5% off most Target purchases at checkout. Target Circle 360 is a paid tier at $99 a year or $10.99 a month. Its main perk is free same-day delivery on orders over $35, which costs other shoppers $9.99 an order, so 10 deliveries a year cover the $99 fee.

Wait to make significant purchases until Target Circle Deal Days, the members-only sales Target held in March, June, and October in 2026, the October one with up to 40% off thousands of items.

Join Target Circle free in the Target app before your next trip.

My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
  • Recent findings suggest that but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
  • Sources indicate that I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

Recent findings suggest that but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

Sources indicate that I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

Recent findings suggest that but a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

Yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

One of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health tech giant that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

Long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

Another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

Sources indicate that so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s new firm, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

The next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

According to recent reports, and wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

It’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

Sources indicate that this is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

It has been revealed that it turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

In many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

Industry observers note that but there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

Many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

Sources indicate that while this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

Recent findings suggest that distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

And while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

Recent findings suggest that so I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

According to recent reports, I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty rapidly in the past.

Recent findings suggest that but on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

Many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

Since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a latest, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term looks again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

Industry observers note that when you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that notes, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the matter, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

In a recent development, the modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

Since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

Many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

More modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

My hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

In a recent development, and it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

It has been revealed that the great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The company that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

Note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

It has been revealed that I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

Wash it in the shade with car soap and two buckets, then vacuum and treat cloth seats and carpet with baking soda and diluted vinegar. Consumer Reports says to expect to pay more than $200 to have a car deep-cleaned inside and out. Neither the wash nor the wipe-down needs pro equipment.

Recent findings suggest that fill one bucket with water and car wash soap, not dish soap, which Consumer Reports warns may strip off the protective wax. Rinse your wash mitt in a second bucket of plain water after each section, so the grit doesn’t scratch the paint.

It has been revealed that wash in the shade from the roof down, since sun can dry the soap into spots before you rinse it. Then dry with microfiber towels, because air-drying can leave mineral spots.

Recent findings suggest that about $40 buys two 5-gallon buckets, car wash soap, a wash mitt, microfiber towels, a dashboard protectant, and an ammonia-free glass cleaner, since ammonia can damage window tint film. Add baking soda and white vinegar from the kitchen, and do the inside in this order.

Leave three jobs to a detailer. Paint correction, which removes scratches and swirl marks, needs a pro’s tools and experience. Stains or smells that outlast the baking soda and vinegar need a detailer’s hot-water carpet cleaner or odor treatment. And before you sell, book a detail only when it costs less than it adds to your car’s resale value.

Recent findings suggest that say four $200 details a year cost you $800 and one $40 kit lasts the year. Doing it yourself saves $760 of that $800, or $190 for each afternoon of work.

It has been revealed that A $40 lamp tagged 30% off costs $28 today and $12 at 70% off, so waiting saves $16 if it’s still on the shelf. Anyone else can buy it in the meantime.

In a recent development, scan the barcode in the Target app before you decide. Stores can take days to put up new stickers, so an item can ring up at a deeper markdown than its sticker shows.

When the shelf is down to one or two in your size or color, buy at 30% or 50%, since waiting saves nothing on an item that’s gone. Target’s price match excludes clearance, so you can’t get the difference back after a later markdown.

According to recent reports, the day after Christmas, holiday lights at 50% off usually reach 70% within the week and 90% soon after, while a popular toy at 30% off can sell out before its next markdown. Hold off on the lights, and buy the toy now.

It has been revealed that start with a Little Free Library, one of the small book boxes anyone can take from or add to. Little Free Library’s map and its free app show boxes near you, though only those their owners registered and chose to list. The organization’s rules don’t require you to leave a book to take one, but keeping a box stocked is up to the people who use it, so bring a few of yours.

It has been revealed that for a specific title, try a book-swap site. On PaperBackSwap, open to U.S. residents over 18, each book you mail to a member who requests it earns a credit. Each credit gets you a paperback or hardcover that another member mails at their expense.

According to recent reports, you pay to mail yours. A typical paperback weighs under a pound and costs $4.39 to send by Media Mail, the Postal Service’s low-cost option for books. PaperBackSwap’s free initiative charges a 99-cent swap fee for each book you request, but printing your postage through the site costs 55 cents and earns you a request with no fee. That puts each book you get at about $4.94 in postage and fees.

For a swap party, ask friends or coworkers to bring books they’ve finished and would recommend. Set them out by genre, and draw numbers so people take turns picking one at a time. Donate the leftover books.

Recent findings suggest that say you have 12 finished paperbacks, each under a pound. Mailing six to PaperBackSwap members who request them, with postage printed through the site, costs $29.64, and the six credits you earn get you six books with no swap fees. Leave the other six in a Little Free Library box over a few visits and take six you’ll read. That’s 12 books you haven’t read for $29.64, about $2.47 each.

List 10 finished books on PaperBackSwap, and its two startup credits, which go to one account per household, get you two books before you mail any.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that amazon Prime costs about half as much for anyone 18 to 24 or in college and for people on SNAP, Medicaid, or other qualifying aid, so check those intends before you pay $139 a year. If another adult in your home also pays full price, cancel one membership and share the one you keep through Amazon Family.

Both discounted plans carry the same core benefits as regular Prime, so paying the full $14.99 a month instead of $7.49 or $6.99 costs $90 to $96 more a year.

Sources indicate that prime Access costs $6.99 a month after a 30-day free trial for upcoming members. It’s open to people on SNAP, Medicaid, Social Security disability, or one of 10 other assistance programs, including public housing and energy aid, and to anyone who passes Amazon’s income check. You upload proof, such as your benefits card or eligibility letter, and reverify every 12 months.

In a recent development, on regular Prime or Prime for Young Adults, pay monthly only if you’ll keep the membership nine months or fewer, such as just for the holidays. Ten months of regular Prime at $14.99 cost $149.90, more than the $139 yearly price, so switch to yearly billing once you know you’ll keep it.

Amazon Family, which replaced Amazon Household, lets a Prime member share free delivery, Prime Video, Amazon Music, and member deals with one other adult in the household, who keeps a separate Amazon account. Two adults paying $139 each can cancel one membership and save $139 a year.

Prime for Young Adults and free trials can’t be shared, so the shared membership has to be regular Prime or Prime Access. And the member who shares Prime must also share a payment method, which the other adult can use for purchases, so set this up only with someone you’d trust with it.

In a home where either adult qualifies for Prime Access, keep that membership, since it covers both of you for $83.88 a year, $55.12 less than one regular annual membership.

Read our Amazon Prime review to see whether the membership is worth its full price.
